summary:
GIBBOUS is an interactive lunar mission design simulator that challenges players to plan, configure and evaluate their own lunar exploration missions using real-world NASA data.

Players take on the role of mission planners, making critical decisions involving launch vehicles, spacecraft architecture, scientific payloads, resource allocation, orbital constraints and lunar landing-site selection. By integrating NASA lunar imagery, elevation data and geographical information into an interactive 3D lunar environment, GIBBOUS allows players to explore the Moon and assess potential landing locations using scientific considerations.

The project addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by transforming complex aerospace mission-planning concepts into an accessible, interactive experience. It combines educational gameplay with real scientific datasets, demonstrating how engineering decisions, available resources and environmental conditions influence the feasibility of a space mission.

GIBBOUS aims to make lunar exploration more understandable and engaging while encouraging interest in aerospace engineering, planetary science and space exploration.
details:
GIBBOUS is a Unity-based lunar mission design simulator developed in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge's Space Mission Design Game challenge.

The simulator places players in the role of aerospace mission planners, allowing them to design and evaluate a lunar exploration mission through a series of interactive configuration stages.

Players make decisions across several aspects of mission design, including:

  • Launch Vehicle Selection: Choosing an appropriate launch system based on mission requirements.
  • Spacecraft Architecture: Configuring the spacecraft and considering its mass, power and operational requirements.
  • Scientific Payload Selection: Selecting scientific instruments and equipment according to mission objectives.
  • Resource Management: Balancing available budgets, mass, power and other mission constraints.
  • Lunar Landing Site Selection: Exploring a 3D representation of the Moon and evaluating potential landing locations using NASA lunar imagery, elevation information and geographical features.
  • Mission Feasibility: Considering orbital conditions, radiation exposure, fuel requirements and other environmental constraints when evaluating mission decisions.

One of GIBBOUS's central features is its interactive lunar environment. Rather than relying entirely on fictional terrain, the project incorporates real lunar observations and geographical information from NASA resources. This provides a scientific foundation for exploring the lunar surface and making informed landing-site decisions.

The project combines game development, scientific data visualisation and aerospace engineering concepts to make complex mission-planning processes more accessible.

GIBBOUS was developed using Unity and C#, with a focus on modular systems, interactive interfaces and the integration of external scientific datasets.

Its intended impact is to encourage interest in space exploration, demonstrate the importance of data-driven engineering decisions and provide an educational experience that introduces players to the challenges involved in planning real lunar missions.

The team considered mission feasibility, scientific accuracy, resource limitations, user accessibility and the balance between educational value and engaging gameplay throughout development.
